/-!
# Conjecture 9.37

by Yu. N. Mukhin

Is a compactly generated inductively prosoluble locally compact group prosoluble?

Conventions. Locally compact groups are Hausdorff. A topological group is *compactly
generated* if it is generated (as a group) by a compact subset. A locally compact group $G$ is
*prosoluble* if it is a projective limit of soluble locally compact groups, that is, every
neighbourhood of the identity contains a closed normal subgroup $N$ with $G/N$ soluble. It is
*inductively prosoluble* if every closed subgroup topologically generated by finitely many
elements is prosoluble.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.name: IsCompactlyGeneratedGroup
blocks.text:
/-- A topological group $G$ is *compactly generated* if there is a compact subset
$K \subseteq G$ with $\langle K \rangle = G$. -/
def IsCompactlyGeneratedGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] : Prop :=
  ∃ K : Set G, IsCompact K ∧ Subgroup.closure K = ⊤

blocks.docstring:
A topological group $G$ is *prosoluble* if every neighbourhood $U$ of the identity contains
a closed normal subgroup $N$ such that the quotient $G/N$ is soluble. For a locally compact
group $G$ this says that $G$ is the projective limit of its soluble quotients $G/N$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: IsSolvable (abstract groups only); no pro-P notions for topological groups in Mathlib
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.37».IsProsolvable
justification.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has pro-soluble (projective limit of soluble groups) for topological groups. Defined as: for every U ∈ 𝓝 1 there is a closed normal subgroup N ⊆ U with `IsSolvable (G ⧸ N)`. For Hausdorff G this is equivalent to G being the projective limit of the soluble groups G/N; abstract solubility of G/N coincides with topological solubility since N is closed (a finite closed normal series with abelian factors exists iff the abstract derived series terminates).

blocks.name: IsProsolvable
blocks.text:
/-- A topological group $G$ is *prosoluble* if every neighbourhood $U$ of the identity contains
a closed normal subgroup $N$ such that the quotient $G/N$ is soluble. For a locally compact
group $G$ this says that $G$ is the projective limit of its soluble quotients $G/N$. -/
def IsProsolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] : Prop :=
  ∀ U ∈ 𝓝 (1 : G), ∃ (N : Subgroup G) (_ : N.Normal),
    IsClosed (N : Set G) ∧ (N : Set G) ⊆ U ∧ IsSolvable (G ⧸ N)

blocks.docstring:
A topological group $G$ is *inductively prosoluble* if every closed subgroup of $G$
that is topologically generated by finitely many elements, that is, every subgroup of the form
$\overline{\langle g_1, \dots, g_n \rangle}$ with the subspace topology, is prosoluble.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Subgroup.topologicalClosure and Subgroup.closure (used as building blocks); nothing for the compound notion
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.37».IsInductivelyProsolvable
justification.why_needed: Bespoke notion from the Kourovka problem: every closed subgroup topologically generated by finitely many elements is prosoluble. Defined as `∀ S : Finset G, IsProsolvable (Subgroup.closure ↑S).topologicalClosure`. (The alternative reading 'every compactly generated closed subgroup is prosoluble' would trivialise the question for compactly generated G, as the decomposition notes point out.)

blocks.name: IsInductivelyProsolvable
blocks.text:
/-- A topological group $G$ is *inductively prosoluble* if every closed subgroup of $G$
that is topologically generated by finitely many elements, that is, every subgroup of the form
$\overline{\langle g_1, \dots, g_n \rangle}$ with the subspace topology, is prosoluble. -/
def IsInductivelyProsolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] :
    Prop :=
  ∀ S : Finset G, IsProsolvable (Subgroup.closure (S : Set G)).topologicalClosure

theorem isSolvable_of_isProsolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
    [DiscreteTopology G] (h : IsProsolvable G) : IsSolvable G := by
  obtain ⟨N, hN, -, hNU, hsol⟩ := h {1} (by simp)
  obtain rfl : N = ⊥ := (Subgroup.eq_bot_iff_forall N).mpr fun x hx => hNU hx
  exact solvable_of_surjective (QuotientGroup.quotientBot (G := G)).surjective

blocks.docstring:
Is a compactly generated inductively prosoluble locally compact group prosoluble?

That is: let $G$ be a (Hausdorff) locally compact group that is generated by a compact
subset and in which every closed subgroup topologically generated by finitely many elements
is prosoluble. Must $G$ itself be prosoluble, i.e. a projective limit of soluble groups?

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question: the Prop is '∀ G locally compact, compactly generated, inductively prosoluble → G prosoluble'; note that 'inductively prosoluble' must mean every closed subgroup topologically generated by finitely many elements is prosoluble (not every compactly generated closed subgroup, which would make the question trivial for compactly generated G), and 'prosoluble' for a locally compact group means a projective limit of soluble locally compact groups (i.e. G/N soluble for closed normal N running over a neighbourhood base of the identity), conventions that the formalizer must pin down explicitly since Mathlib has no such notions.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates are mathematically equivalent and match the decomposition table's conventions: G a Hausdorff locally compact topological group; compactly generated = algebraically generated by a compact set (c04's topological-closure variant is equivalent for locally compact groups); prosoluble = every identity neighbourhood contains a closed normal N with G/N soluble (= projective limit of soluble locally compact groups; abstract and topological solubility coincide for Hausdorff quotients); inductively prosoluble = every closure⟨S⟩, S finite, prosoluble in the subspace topology (the non-trivialising reading; c03/c04/c05/c07's 'closed H with a dense finitely generated subgroup' phrasing is equivalent). Statement is `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G, …` with all quantifiers after answer, matching the Kourovka files. Verified with pp.explicit that the Normal witness is the instance used for G ⧸ N and that the subgroup carries the subspace topology. c01 chosen for the cleanest naming (c03/c04/c05's `IsCompactlyGenerated` shadows Mathlib's lattice class of the same name and only works by overload disambiguation; c04 uses awkward implicit-argument `(G := G)` calls), explicit-argument definitions, and three proven API lemmas testing the bespoke definitions. Edits: sharpened the docstrings of the module and of `IsProsolvable` (the 'neighbourhood base' phrasing was ambiguous) and stated the subspace-topology convention in `IsInductivelyProsolvable`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.37

by Yu. N. Mukhin

Is a compactly generated inductively prosoluble locally compact group prosoluble?

Conventions. Locally compact groups are Hausdorff. A topological group is *compactly
generated* if it is generated (as a group) by a compact subset. A locally compact group $G$ is
*prosoluble* if it is a projective limit of soluble locally compact groups, that is, every
neighbourhood of the identity contains a closed normal subgroup $N$ with $G/N$ soluble. It is
*inductively prosoluble* if every closed subgroup topologically generated by finitely many
elements is prosoluble.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open Topology

namespace Kourovka.«9.37»

/-- A topological group $G$ is *compactly generated* if there is a compact subset
$K \subseteq G$ with $\langle K \rangle = G$. -/
def IsCompactlyGeneratedGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] : Prop :=
  ∃ K : Set G, IsCompact K ∧ Subgroup.closure K = ⊤

/-- A topological group $G$ is *prosoluble* if every neighbourhood $U$ of the identity contains
a closed normal subgroup $N$ such that the quotient $G/N$ is soluble. For a locally compact
group $G$ this says that $G$ is the projective limit of its soluble quotients $G/N$. -/
def IsProsolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] : Prop :=
  ∀ U ∈ 𝓝 (1 : G), ∃ (N : Subgroup G) (_ : N.Normal),
    IsClosed (N : Set G) ∧ (N : Set G) ⊆ U ∧ IsSolvable (G ⧸ N)

/-- A topological group $G$ is *inductively prosoluble* if every closed subgroup of $G$
that is topologically generated by finitely many elements, that is, every subgroup of the form
$\overline{\langle g_1, \dots, g_n \rangle}$ with the subspace topology, is prosoluble. -/
def IsInductivelyProsolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] :
    Prop :=
  ∀ S : Finset G, IsProsolvable (Subgroup.closure (S : Set G)).topologicalClosure

/-- A compact group is compactly generated. -/
@[category API, AMS 22]
theorem isCompactlyGeneratedGroup_of_compactSpace (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
    [CompactSpace G] : IsCompactlyGeneratedGroup G :=
  ⟨Set.univ, isCompact_univ, Subgroup.closure_univ⟩

/-- A soluble $T_1$ topological group is prosoluble. -/
@[category API, AMS 22]
theorem isProsolvable_of_isSolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [T1Space G]
    [IsSolvable G] : IsProsolvable G := fun U hU =>
  ⟨⊥, inferInstance, by simp, by simpa using mem_of_mem_nhds hU, inferInstance⟩

/-- A discrete prosoluble group is soluble. -/
@[category API, AMS 22]
theorem isSolvable_of_isProsolvable (G : Type*) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
    [DiscreteTopology G] (h : IsProsolvable G) : IsSolvable G := by
  obtain ⟨N, hN, -, hNU, hsol⟩ := h {1} (by simp)
  obtain rfl : N = ⊥ := (Subgroup.eq_bot_iff_forall N).mpr fun x hx => hNU hx
  exact solvable_of_surjective (QuotientGroup.quotientBot (G := G)).surjective

/--
Is a compactly generated inductively prosoluble locally compact group prosoluble?

That is: let $G$ be a (Hausdorff) locally compact group that is generated by a compact
subset and in which every closed subgroup topologically generated by finitely many elements
is prosoluble. Must $G$ itself be prosoluble, i.e. a projective limit of soluble groups?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka.«9.37» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [T2Space G]
      [LocallyCompactSpace G],
      IsCompactlyGeneratedGroup G → IsInductivelyProsolvable G → IsProsolvable G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.37»

items: Topological groups are assumed Hausdorff (`T2Space G`), the standard convention for locally compact groups. Non-Hausdorff groups reduce to their Hausdorff quotient by the closure of {1} for all three notions, so the assumption is harmless, but a reviewer should confirm it is wanted.

'Prosoluble' is read as a projective limit of soluble (not necessarily discrete or Lie) groups: closed normal N with G/N soluble form a neighbourhood base of 1. In a locally compact group such N are eventually compact, so this agrees with the 'compact normal subgroups with trivial intersection' formulation. If the notebook intended pro-(finite soluble) (i.e. prosoluble profinite quotients only), the statement would differ; the decomposition table specifies the former.
Solubility of G/N is Mathlib's abstract `IsSolvable`; for closed N this is equivalent to topological solubility (closed derived series), so no convention issue arises.

'Inductively prosoluble' quantifies over closed subgroups `closure⟨S⟩` for finite S (`Finset G`), each with the subspace topology, per the decomposition notes. This is equivalent to G being a directed union of closed prosoluble subgroups (the 'inductive limit' reading), since closed subgroups of prosoluble locally compact groups are prosoluble.
'Compactly generated' means algebraically generated by a compact subset (⟨K⟩ = G), not the topological k-space notion.
Groups are quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the other Kourovka files.
Three short `@[category API]` lemmas test the definitions: compact ⇒ compactly generated; soluble T₁ group ⇒ prosoluble; discrete prosoluble ⇒ soluble.

reviewer_notes: The source is a one-line question with undefined technical terms; the formalization pins the conventions the decomposition table specifies and states them in the docstrings. Residual risk (reflected in the confidence): Mukhin's 'prosoluble' might conceivably mean 'projective limit of soluble *Lie* groups' rather than of soluble locally compact groups; the two notions differ in general (e.g. ℚ_p ⋊ ℤ is soluble but not pro-Lie in the compact-kernel sense). The table specifies the latter reading, all eight candidates used it, and it is the natural reading of 'pro-X' in the Russian locally-compact-group literature. Compact-generation (algebraic vs topological) and closed-vs-compact kernels are immaterial for locally compact groups. Note c08's stated argument for rejecting the 'open normal subgroups' reading (ℝ as counterexample) is flawed—closure⟨1, √2⟩ = ℝ is not prosoluble in that sense either—but its conclusion (that reading is wrong, as it forces total disconnectedness and is not what 'projective limit' means) is correct. Hausdorff (T2Space) is assumed, the standard convention for locally compact groups. Final file compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning; the API lemmas are fully proved.
